title: OmniVia Chat Runtime Contract v1 - Read projections
description: Closes CGAP-042-007 (branch path, pinned-snapshot, sibling, branch-list and lazy-descendant queries) and freezes the W2 read-projection surface named by the Chat technical delivery specification §10 and §12.6: paginated Conversation list/search, actor/selected-path Conversation snapshot, stable-anchor Message/Part paging. Every query is authorised at read time (REF-042 §11.1, §15.1) and returns only accessible content; an inaccessible required ancestor fails the containing query closed rather than partially assembling a path (REF-042 §11.1 step 4, REF042-RULE-013). Every list and page query is bounded and cursor-paginated (`PageSize`, `OpaqueCursor`); no query loads an unbounded graph (REF-042 §11.3, §26.2).

DivergenceMetadata.title: DivergenceMetadata
DivergenceMetadata.description: Lightweight sibling-position metadata at one visible divergence point, without loading inactive siblings' content (REF-042 §11.3, §16.2). Closes part of CGAP-042-007.

selectedOrdinal.description: 1-based position of this Message within its sibling set (REF-042 §10.2).

BranchPathQuery.title: BranchPathQuery
BranchPathQuery.description: Reconstructs one branch path root-to-head, or a pinned snapshot when `pinnedGraphRevision` and `pinnedHeadMessageId` are supplied together (REF-042 §11.1, §11.2). Closes CGAP-042-007.

BranchPathResult.title: BranchPathResult
BranchPathResult.description: REF-042 Appendix D `ConversationThreadProjection`, disposable and rebuildable, never itself the authoritative graph.

divergenceMetadataByMessageId.description: Keyed by `messageId` (REF-042 §16.2). Present only for visible Messages belonging to a sibling set with more than one member.

generationJobIds.description: The selected branch's complete durable Generation Job projection at `graphRevision`, not merely the ids the path's result Messages reference: a job is durable from the moment the `SubmitMessage` that triggers it commits, so a `queued` or `running` job with no result Message yet is listed here too. Deterministically ordered and duplicate-free; complete or refused, never truncated to fit `maxItems`.

BranchListQuery.title: BranchListQuery
BranchListQuery.description: Lists branches for one Conversation (REF-042 §10.3, §16). Closes part of CGAP-042-007.

BranchSummary.title: BranchSummary
BranchSummary.description: Lightweight branch-list row, not the full `MessageBranch` record.

DescendantsQuery.title: DescendantsQuery
DescendantsQuery.description: Lazily loads inactive descendants from a Message, for a divergence control expanded by the user (REF-042 §11.3, §16.2). Closes part of CGAP-042-007.

ConversationListQuery.title: ConversationListQuery
ConversationListQuery.description: Paginated Conversation list and search (Chat technical delivery specification §10). Not part of CGAP-042-007; freezes the W2 read surface only.

searchText.description: Untrusted search text matched against canonical Message content, never truncated rendered DOM (REF-042 §19.1).

matchedMessageId.description: Present only for a search result; identifies the exact branch-scoped match (REF-042 §19.2).

ConversationSnapshotQuery.title: ConversationSnapshotQuery
ConversationSnapshotQuery.description: The actor's selected-path Conversation snapshot (Chat technical delivery specification §10): `Conversation` plus the actor's resolved active branch path in one bounded read.

ToolCallProjection.title: ToolCallProjection
ToolCallProjection.description:
One governed tool call of a conversation, as a snapshot publishes it (C8). Identity, lifecycle state and timing are conversation state and go to any reader who may read the conversation -- a turn blocked on a tool call is a fact about the conversation, and hiding it would leave a reader unable to explain why nothing is happening. Everything a REVIEWER needs is in `review`, which is projected only to an actor the wait's authorised-responder policy admits.

Deliberately absent: the tool's arguments, in any form. The decision command requires a reviewer to echo `targetActionDigest` and `targetResourceRevision`, and `review.actionSummary` carries the closed, bounded, registry-DERIVED description of the action the wait is bound to, so a reviewer can decide without them. Publishing arguments would be this bundle's first outbound disclosure of tool inputs; adding them later is additive, and removing them would not be. Also absent, permanently: `resumeTokenDigest`, `answerDigest` and `sensitiveAnswerCiphertextDigest`. Each is a digest of a secret, and a digest of a short secret is a guessing oracle rather than a protection.

generationJobId.description: The generation job this call was proposed within, where the call names one.

registryRef.description: The governed tool registry entry this call was admitted against.

state.description: The call's lifecycle state. An open code, because the lifecycle is Core's and a consumer that meets an unfamiliar state must display it inertly rather than refuse the snapshot.

failureCode.description: Present only on a call that failed.

finishedAt.description: Present only once the call reached a terminal state.

review.description:
The open wait on this call, projected ONLY to an actor its authorised-responder policy admits. Absent means either that there is no wait or that this reader may not answer it, and the two are deliberately indistinguishable: a reader who could tell them apart would learn who may review, which is not theirs to know.

What the responder READS is the closed document for the wait's own kind, and the two are mutually exclusive: an `approval` or `policy_pause` carries `actionSummary`, a `human_input` carries `prompt`, and the `allOf` below refuses the other one in each case. The binding is total over the closed `kind`, so neither member can arrive labelled as the other. Both are OPTIONAL rather than required: a wait whose stored document does not satisfy its closed shape projects NEITHER member, which is the fail-closed answer for a row written before these shapes existed -- a responder with nothing to read cannot approve, and that is correct, where publishing unvalidated prose as `actionSummary` would not be.

kind.description: The wait kind, exactly migration 0033's own CHECK vocabulary. A tool Review opens an `approval`; `tool_review` is the COMMAND name, not the wait kind, and stating it here would refuse a genuine document.

requestVersion.description: The wait version a decision must state as `expectedRequestVersion`. A decision against a superseded version is refused.

targetActionDigest.description: The action digest a decision must echo, where the wait carries one.

targetResourceRevision.description: The resource revision a decision must echo, where the wait carries one.

ToolActionSummary.title: ToolActionSummary
ToolActionSummary.description:
What an authorised responder is shown about the action a Review would authorise (C8). DERIVED, never supplied: `service/chat_tool_lifecycle.derive_action_summary` builds it from the governed tool's own registered `ToolActionSummary` descriptor applied to the EXACT post-policy arguments the call would execute, and `request_tool_review` refuses to open a Review it cannot derive. This replaced an open `prompt` object the caller wrote, which meant the sentence shown to the person approving an action and the arguments that action would run were two independent values nobody compared -- a caller could ask "Append to notes.md?" while the arguments named another file entirely, and the Review would have been of the sentence.

STILL NOT THE ARGUMENTS. The descriptor names which argument KEYS are material and safe to show; every value here came out of the post-policy record, so the summary cannot describe an action other than the one bound to the wait's `targetActionDigest`, but it is a bounded projection of that record and never the record. `value` admits only a bounded scalar, so no nested object can arrive under a name that says it is safe, and the credential check that guards every other chat tool document guards this one too: a summary carrying credential-like text is refused rather than redacted, because post-policy arguments that contain any cannot be recorded in the first place.

operation.description: The action, in the governed registry's own words -- a registered code, not prose a caller chose for this one call.

resource.description: The resource the action affects, read from the post-policy argument the descriptor names. Distinct from `ToolCallProjection.review.targetResourceRef`, which is the wait's revision-checked target: this is what the action's own arguments say it will touch, and a responder comparing the two is comparing exactly what the Review is for.

parameters.description: The further post-policy arguments the registry declared material and safe to show, in the descriptor's own order. Each `name` appears once; Core enforces that, since `uniqueItems` would only catch two identical pairs.

withheldParameters.description: How many of the call's post-policy arguments this summary does NOT show. The redaction fact, stated rather than inferred: a responder who sees three of seven arguments is told so, where silence invites them to read a partial summary as the whole action.

ToolActionSummaryParameter.title: ToolActionSummaryParameter
ToolActionSummaryParameter.description: One material, safe post-policy argument of a summarised action: a bounded name and a bounded SCALAR value. Never an object or an array -- that is how the whole argument record would arrive under a name claiming to be one safe field.

name.description: The post-policy argument key, as the governed tool registered it.

value.description: The value that argument carries in the exact post-policy record. `maxLength` bounds the string case; numbers are finite and restricted to the exact-integer range shared by Python and JavaScript, so a host cannot display a rounded integer different from the argument being reviewed.

HumanInputPrompt.title: HumanInputPrompt
HumanInputPrompt.description:
The closed, renderable question one `human_input` wait was opened with (C8). CLOSED because two things depend on the shape: a renderer has to draw visible fields from it, and `SubmitHumanInput`'s answer has to be checked against it in Core before the wait settles. The open object this replaced could be drawn only as raw JSON, and an answer to it could be validated against nothing at all -- "the shape is the asking tool's business" meant no authority held the shape.

`service/chat_tool_review.validate_human_input_prompt` enforces exactly this when the request opens AND again before it is answered or projected, and `validate_human_input_answer` checks the answer field by field: unknown, missing-required, wrong-typed, off-option and over-bound answers are each refused, by a refusal that names the FIELD and the RULE and never the value. The answer itself remains non-durable -- only its digest and canonical byte count are stored -- and `maxAnswerBytes` still bounds the whole of it.

promptId.description: The asking authority's stable identifier for this prompt, so a renderer and an answer can name the same question across a resnapshot.

title.description: The visible question. Bounded, because it is drawn in a form and not a document.

fields.description: The visible fields, in display order. At least one -- a prompt with no field is a question nothing can answer. Each `fieldId` appears once; Core enforces that.

maxAnswerBytes.description: This request's own ceiling on the whole answer, as canonical JSON counted in UTF-8 bytes. Defaults to 4096 when absent; the bundle ceiling `MAX_ANSWER_BYTES` (16384) applies whatever this says, so a document valid here can still be refused by the wait that receives it.

HumanInputPromptField.title: HumanInputPromptField
HumanInputPromptField.description: One visible field of a `HumanInputPrompt`, and the whole rule its answer value is checked against. `text` carries `maxLength` (default 512), `choice` carries `options`, `boolean` carries neither, and the `allOf` below refuses the other type's constraint: a field stating a bound belonging to a type it is not would be drawn one way by a renderer that read the bound and another by one that read the type, which is two different forms on one prompt.

fieldId.description: The stable identifier this field's answer is keyed by. An answer is an object of `fieldId` to value, so these are the only keys it may carry.

label.description: The visible label for this field.

type.description: The field's value type, closed at three. Each has exactly one answer rule: a boolean takes a JSON boolean, a choice takes one of its own `options` values, and text takes a string of 1 to `maxLength` characters.

required.description: Whether an answer must carry this field. Absent means required: a prompt that forgot to say is asking for the field, and treating silence as optional would settle a wait on an answer that skipped the question.

maxLength.description: A `text` field's character bound. Permitted only on `text`; defaults to 512.

options.description: A `choice` field's offered values, in display order. Required on `choice` and permitted on nothing else; each `value` appears once, which Core enforces.

HumanInputPromptOption.title: HumanInputPromptOption
HumanInputPromptOption.description: One offered value of a `choice` field: the exact string an answer may carry, and the label shown for it.

value.description: The exact value an answer must equal to select this option.

label.description: The visible label for this option.

QueuedSubmissionProjection.title: QueuedSubmissionProjection
QueuedSubmissionProjection.description: The authenticated actor's own active (`queued`) offline-queue submission, joined to its `omnivia_chat_queue_order_projection` row (W5 GB-05). Carries two distinct optimistic tokens on purpose: `version` is the submission's own content token (`UpdateQueuedSubmission.expectedVersion`), `orderVersion` is the order projection's (`ReorderQueuedSubmission.expectedVersion`); they advance independently and neither substitutes for the other. `attachmentReferences`/`contextReferences` are honestly empty and `targetReference` honestly absent for the reference/target subset this build serves. `generationJobId` is the row's own correlated job where one already exists, identity only. Never exposes claim owner, sanitized internal detail or idempotency key -- those are execution-claim internals, not actor-facing queue state.

generationJobId.description: The Generation Job already opened for this row, absent until one exists. A drained row keeps `state: queued` until the generation claimant advances it, so this is what tells a row still awaiting submission apart from one already handed to generation -- without it a reconnecting actor cannot avoid a duplicate drain attempt, and edit eligibility is dishonest. The queue id is Core-derived as `<source command id>.sub` and the job `SubmitMessage.fromQueuedSubmissionId` opens for it as `<source command id>.gen`; the correlation is that exact replacement, verified against a real job in the same workspace, conversation and branch. Never inferred from an id that convention did not derive, never names a missing or foreign job, and never carries claim or execution state.

branch.description: The durable MessageBranch record the resolved `path` was taken from (REF-042 §7.5). Optional, so a snapshot a consumer already accepts stays valid; present wherever the answering authority holds the record, because `headVersion` is the optimistic token a later SubmitMessage must state and `path` is a disposable projection that does not carry it (REF-042 §15.4, §21.4). Never a second branch identity: `branchId` here is `path.branchId`, and `currentHeadMessageId` is `path.headMessageId`.

queuedSubmissions.description: The authenticated actor's own active queued submissions, ordered by `position` then `queuedSubmissionId` (W5 GB-05). Optional and compatible: an existing snapshot consumer that has never seen this field stays valid, and its absence here means the actor's active queue is empty, not that it was skipped. The answering authority MUST either state the actor's complete active queue or fail the whole snapshot closed (`size_limit_exceeded`) rather than publish a partial one bounded by this array's own `maxItems`.

composerDrafts.description: The authenticated actor's own active ComposerDrafts for this conversation at the queried device, one per `ComposerDraftMode`, ordered by `mode` then `draftId` (C5A). Optional and compatible: an existing snapshot consumer that has never seen this field stays valid, and its absence here means the actor holds no active draft, not that it was skipped. A draft is composition state, never a committed Message fact (REF-042 §7.8); its `version` is the optimistic token a later SaveDraft's `expectedVersion` states. The mode vocabulary is closed at three, so no snapshot can be partial: the answering authority either states every active draft or fails the whole snapshot closed.

toolCalls.description: This conversation's governed tool calls, oldest first by creation instant then `toolCallId` (C8). Optional and compatible: an existing snapshot consumer that has never seen this field stays valid, and its absence means the conversation has run no tool call, not that it was skipped. A call's `review` member is present ONLY for an actor the wait's own authorised-responder policy admits -- the same actor-scoped shape `composerDrafts` and `directions` already use -- so a reader who may not answer a wait learns that the turn is waiting and nothing about what it is waiting on. `toolCallsTruncated` says whether this array is the complete set.

toolCallsTruncated.description: Whether `toolCalls` was bounded by its own `maxItems` (C8). Stated rather than inferred: a consumer cannot tell a conversation with exactly 64 calls from one with more, and a snapshot that quietly shortened is the defect this names.

generationJobs.description: The complete durable Generation Job projection for this snapshot's selected branch (C6), ordered by `createdAt` then `jobId`, each carrying its real `version` control token. REQUIRED (C6, bridge/wire 2.0): always present, an empty array when the branch has no Generation Job, so a snapshot that omits it is invalid rather than silently incomplete; a snapshot without it is a pre-C6 document. The answering authority MUST either state every Job of the selected branch or fail the whole snapshot closed (`size_limit_exceeded`) rather than publish a partial list bounded by this array's own `maxItems`; it is the same set `path.generationJobIds` names.

directions.description: The authenticated actor's own Directions (C6) on the Generation Jobs `generationJobs` states, in any Direction state, ordered by `jobId`, then `jobSequence`, then `directionId`. Actor-scoped: every entry's `actorId` is the snapshot's own `viewState.actorId` and every entry's `jobId` names a Job listed in `generationJobs`, never another actor's Direction or a Job the snapshot does not state. REQUIRED (C6, bridge/wire 2.0): always present, an empty array when the actor authored no Direction on those Jobs, so an omitted `directions` is invalid rather than read as "none". The answering authority MUST either state the actor's complete set or fail the whole snapshot closed (`size_limit_exceeded`) rather than publish a partial one.

MessagePageQuery.title: MessagePageQuery
MessagePageQuery.description: Stable-anchor Message and Message Part paging (Chat technical delivery specification §10). `anchorMessageId` absent means page from the branch head.

ComposerDraftQuery.title: ComposerDraftQuery
ComposerDraftQuery.description: Reads back a saved ComposerDraft, for example after reconnect (viewstate.schema.json#/$defs/ComposerDraft).

EvidencePreviewQuery.title: EvidencePreviewQuery
EvidencePreviewQuery.description: Looks up a display-safe preview for one Evidence record by its authorised stable `EvidenceReference` (REF-034 §5.1, §8.2). Reuses Evidence identity by reference only; never redefines REF-034 authority or duplicates Evidence content storage.

EvidencePreviewResult.title: EvidencePreviewResult
EvidencePreviewResult.description: A structured, display-safe preview projection. Never a raw Evidence content dump, raw store error or policy-internal detail.

safeSummary.description: Present only when `outcome` is `available` (REF-034 §5.9-§5.10 content classes summarised safely).

sourceMessageId.description: Present when this Evidence traces to a Chat Message (REF-042 §19.5 L0 Evidence).
